```{=html}
<h1 class="gcpp-hero__h1">NAS&#8209;Pakistan Track</h1>
```

::: {.gcpp-hero__lede}
NASP seeks to develop original, dedicated, and rigorous scholarship on Pakistan among a new generation of serious Indian researchers. This fellowship is particularly relevant because familiarity is often mistaken for understanding: despite Pakistan's centrality to India's strategic mindset, much of the discourse is shaped by assumptions, stereotypes, and episodic crises rather than sustained scholarship.
:::
:::

::: {.gcpp-hero__aside}
::: {.eyebrow}
Quick facts
:::
| | |
|---|---|
| **DOMAIN**    | Pakistan studies |
| **COURSE**    | ECCs + GCPP special sessions |
| **PROPOSAL**  | 1,000–1,500 words + 500–800-word SoP |
| **FELLOWS**   | Up to 6 per cohort |
:::
:::
:::

```{=html}
<!-- ============ RESEARCH DOMAINS ============ -->
<div class="gcpp-section">
  <div class="gcpp-container">
    <span class="eyebrow">Research domains</span>
    <h2 class="gcpp-h2">Propose your own topic</h2>
    <p class="nasx-prose" style="margin-bottom:24px;">This is a general call for research proposals. Fellows are not required to work on pre-assigned themes. You are encouraged to propose a topic within the broad domain of Pakistan studies, including (but not limited to) the following areas.</p>
    <ul class="unit-list">
      <li><span class="u">P.01</span> The Pakistan military, defence policy, and strategic culture</li>
      <li><span class="u">P.02</span> Pakistan as a geostrategic rentier state and the political economy of security</li>
      <li><span class="u">P.03</span> Pakistan's defence industry, arms imports and exports, and military modernisation</li>
      <li><span class="u">P.04</span> Identity formation, federalism, ethnic politics, and sub-national movements</li>
      <li><span class="u">P.05</span> The military-jihadi complex, militancy, and violent extremism</li>
      <li><span class="u">P.06</span> Pakistan's maritime strategy, sea power, and the Indian Ocean</li>
      <li><span class="u">P.07</span> The judiciary, constitutional politics, and institutional evolution</li>
      <li><span class="u">P.08</span> Pakistan's economy, governance, and domestic political developments</li>
    </ul>
    <p class="nasx-prose" style="margin-top:24px;">Research proposals may also explore emerging issues such as technology, climate, demographics, information ecosystems, or other themes relevant to understanding contemporary Pakistan.</p>
    <p class="nasx-prose" style="margin-top:16px;">As part of the fellowship, fellows can choose to enrol in any of the <strong>ECCs</strong> running in that period, and will have access to special <strong>GCPP</strong> sessions by guest lecturers on Pakistan studies.</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="gcpp-section">

    <h2 class="gcpp-h2">How to apply</h2>
    <div class="apply-list no-codes">
      <div class="apply-item">
        <div class="body">
          <h3>Proposal & Statement of Purpose</h3>
          <p>Submit a research proposal of 1,000–1,500 words outlining the topic, the research questions, and the approach. Proposals should clearly identify the gap in existing scholarship and explain why the topic merits sustained attention. Applicants will also submit a 500–800-word Statement of Purpose explaining their reasons for pursuing a fellowship in this domain. Only one author per proposal will be accepted.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="apply-item">
        <div class="body">
          <h3>Interviews</h3>
          <p>Submitted proposals undergo internal review, and applicants whose proposals are shortlisted will be invited to a virtual interview.</p>
        </div>

      <div class="apply-item">
```
